filename: Catastrophic “hyperclustering” and recurrent losses_ diagnosing U.S. flood insurance insolvency triggers.pdf
title: Catastrophic “hyperclustering” and recurrent losses: diagnosing U.S. flood insurance insolvency triggers
code_availability: We provide open access code for all processes in this manuscript in the following GitHub repository: https://github.com/adamnayak/Hyperclusters.
testbed_rationale: The study conducts spatiotemporal clustering of disaster insurance loss records and game-theoretic risk indexing rather than developing or evaluating atmospheric/oceanic physical parameterizations or emulators.
pain_points: Unavailability of public household-level premium data linked to historical NFIP claims and changes in insured assets over time limits normalization approaches.
Claim amounts and specific loss dates for multiple loss properties are not publicly available.
Sensitivity and difficulty in parameterizing density-based spatiotemporal clustering (thresholds for space, time, and point thresholds in ST-DBSCAN).
Heavy-tailed, fat-tailed catastrophic risk distributions that standard expected-value pricing models are not structurally designed to buffer.
extraction_notes: The paper uses unsupervised machine learning (ST-DBSCAN and k-means) together with the Analytic Hierarchy Process, entropy weighting, and game theory to diagnose NFIP insolvency drivers. Cloud computing was supported by the LEAP NSF STC.
